standard_prerequisites: Chapter Situation situation-finitely-generated (source lines 1485-1496): K = F(alpha_1..alpha_n) finite, tower K_i = F(alpha_1..alpha_i), P_i the minimal polynomial of alpha_i over K_{i-1}, algebraic closure overline{F} fixed

Universal property of quotient rings: a homomorphism out of K_{i-1}[x]/(P_i) over K_{i-1} is the same as a choice of a root of P_i^{phi_{i-1}} in the target; this is also why each step map phi_i exists and is unique

The section paragraph immediately preceding the lemma (source lines 1499-1505): a morphism phi: K -> overline{F} yields step maps phi_i and phi(alpha_i) is a root of the conjugated polynomial P_i^{phi_{i-1}}
core_obligations: Left to right: a morphism phi: K = K_n -> overline{F} restricts to step maps phi_i, and the tuple (phi(alpha_1), ..., phi(alpha_n)) satisfies the recursive root conditions (1)-(4) of the statement

Right to left: given a tuple satisfying (1)-(4), the step maps phi_i exist and are unique (universal property of K_i = K_{i-1}[x]/(P_i)), and composing gives a unique phi: K -> overline{F} with phi(alpha_i) = beta_i
Uniqueness at every step makes the two constructions mutually inverse, so the correspondence is a bijection
proof_roadmap: Restrict a morphism down the tower to get a compatible tuple
Build the morphism back up the tower from a tuple and close by uniqueness
